script: Sharks can sense the tiny electric fields made by other animals' muscles. They do it with jelly-filled pores on their snouts, called the ampullae of Lorenzini. This lets them find fish hiding under the sand, even without seeing them. The pores are named after Stefano Lorenzini, who described them in 1678. Rays, close relatives of sharks, have the same electric sense. Follow Pixel Abyss for more strange facts from the deep.
